title: 6 Misconceptions Of Smart Classroom Management https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2019/06/08/smart-classroom-management-misconceptions/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin directly addresses six common misconceptions about Smart Classroom Management, aiming to correct misunderstandings from comments and emails. He clarifies that he is a current, practicing public school teacher, not a former one; that SCM's focus on solutions is not intended to blame teachers, who bear no responsibility for student misbehavior; and that the approach is neither too tough (it enforces firm, nonnegotiable boundaries) nor too soft (it explicitly rejects intimidation, scolding, and raised voices). He also responds to the seemingly contradictory claims that SCM is both too complex and too simple, pointing to condensed resources like his book and e-guides while affirming the underlying philosophy — building a classroom students love — is simple even if it requires real study to apply well.
points: Clarifies he is a current, practicing public school teacher, not a former one, and still uses SCM strategies daily.
States SCM does not blame teachers for misbehavior, since responsibility for behavior rests with students, but solutions rest with teachers.
Rejects both 'too tough' and 'too soft' criticisms, explicitly disavowing intimidation, scolding, or raised voices as effective tools.
Addresses claims of being both too complex and too simple, pointing to condensed resources for readers overwhelmed by the full archive.
Frames the SCM philosophy as fundamentally simple — building a classroom students love — even though applying it well requires real study.
quotes: Although I no longer need to teach, I have no plans of giving it up.
Students are 100% responsible for their behavior, without a doubt. However, the solutions to misbehavior, disrespect, and the like reside with the teacher.
At SCM, we do not in any circumstance advocate intimidation . No scolding. No glaring. No raising your voice.
It’s your consistent pleasantness and kindness, combined with a single-minded commitment to your classroom management plan, that gives you the leverage to manage any classroom.

Instead of charts, tokens, external rewards , bribery, manipulation, and the like, instead of trying to convince, coerce, or beg students to behave, we believe in creating a classroom they love being part of.
You have to spend some time reading and studying to ensure you really understand the SCM way and how to apply it in your classroom.
